title: Shelve look-alike drug cartons apart, names facing the front
instruction: Stand the four drug cartons upright in the shelf pockets, one per pocket, with a wide face toward the black front lip. The red and blue cartons are look-alike drugs: never put them in the same or neighbouring pockets.
context: Medication-safety guidance tells pharmacies to keep look-alike, sound-alike drugs apart on the shelf and to shelve them name-forward, because side-by-side look-alikes cause wrong-drug picks; the nearest-pockets-first placement puts the pair side by side. Done by: pharmacy technicians, pharmacy aides, hospital stores staff.
setup: A dark grey plastic shelf rack is fixed to the table between the arms, its centre 28 cm in front of the arm bases: one row of six open pockets from left to right, each 46 x 46 mm inside, 52 mm apart centre to centre, with a 4 mm floor and 6 mm thick lips and dividers rising 12 mm above the floor; outside 318 mm left to right and 58 mm front to back. The lip nearest the arms is black. The pockets are numbered 1 to 6 from the robot's left. Four cardboard drug cartons (40 mm wide, 24 mm deep, 60 mm tall, 60 g each, the drug name printed on both 40 x 60 mm faces) stand upright on the table with their wide faces turned to the sides (the 40 mm side pointing away from the arms): a red and a blue carton 30 cm left of centre, in front of the left arm, their centres 20 and 32 cm in front of the arm bases; a green and a yellow carton 30 cm right of centre, in front of the right arm, at 20 and 32 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A carton is shelved when its centre is inside a pocket's 46 x 46 mm inside, it is tilted at most 10 degrees and its bottom is within 5 mm of the pocket floor: 0.15 each, if no other shelved carton is in the same pocket. A shelved carton earns 0.10 more if a wide face points to the front lip within 20 degrees (either wide face counts). All four shelved and facing the front: 1.0. The score is 0 if the red and blue cartons' centres are over the same or neighbouring pockets, each pocket owning a 52 mm wide band across the rack's full 58 mm depth, with each of the two either standing on another carton (its bottom within 10 mm of that carton's top, their outlines overlapping seen from above), however high the stack, or with its bottom less than 70 mm above the pocket floor (in a pocket, on the lips or on a shelved carton), at any tilt. Only a carton in the air over the rack, its bottom 70 mm or more above the pocket floor with no carton under it (as when carried in the gripper), does not count for this rule; it earns nothing itself.
reset_notes: Take the cartons out of the rack and stand them back at their four marks on the table, wide faces turned to the sides; tape outlines make this quick. The rack stays clamped in place.
fidelity: Approximate: each carton is one solid box, and colour stands in for the printed name, so the look-alikes are told apart by colour rather than by reading similar names; the vial inside is not modelled. The rack is fixed (clamp it for real trials). Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than cardboard on plastic.
